props.gloss_en: in truth they said: a son may bless for his father, a slave for his master, a woman for her husband
but the Sages said: may a curse come upon a man whose wife and children bless for him
Rava: great halakhot can be learned from the custom of Hallel
it is a mitzva to answer 'Halleluyah'
Rava's source: he says 'Halleluyah' and they say 'Halleluyah'
if an adult leads him [in Hallel], he answers after him 'Halleluyah' (the mishna's clause, same content)
Rava's source: he says 'Praise, servants of the Lord' and they say 'Halleluyah'
it is a mitzva to answer the chapter-heads
Rava's source: he says 'Give thanks to the Lord' and they say 'Give thanks to the Lord'
if a minor leads him, they answer after him what he says
Rava's source: he says 'Lord, please save' and they repeat 'Lord, please save'
one who comes to double [a verse] doubles it
Rava's source: he says 'Lord, please prosper' and they repeat 'Lord, please prosper'
one who hears is as one who answers
Rava's source: he says 'Blessed is he who comes' and they say 'in the name of the Lord'
one who heard and did not answer has discharged [his obligation]
Bar Kappara: from where that one who hears is as one who answers? 'the words which Josiah read' (Melakhim II 22:16) -- yet Shaphan read them (22:10); hence one who hears is as one who reads
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: 'because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the Lord when you heard' (Melakhim II 22:19) -- 'when you heard', not 'when you read'
Rava: one should not say 'Blessed is he who comes' and then 'in the name of the Lord', but both together
Rav Safra: Moshe, are you speaking well?! there and here it is the conclusion of the matter, and we have no problem with it [pausing is fine]
Rava: one should not say 'May His great name' and then 'be blessed', but together
Rav Safra: Moshe, are you speaking well?! there and here it is the conclusion of the matter, and we have no problem with it
